correctness.rationale: For two independent outer and two independent inner circle points, outer points are always extreme. Mutual exclusivity of the two possible inner-point containment failures reduces Q=1-2H. The bearing map t=theta-arcsin(r sin theta) has the stated positive Jacobian; inner-to-inner bearing is uniform on inward semicircle. Unique-semicircle-anchor integration gives exactly Q=1/2+8/pi^3 int x arcsin(r sin x)+4/pi^3 int arcsin^2(r sin x). Direct differentiation makes Q strictly increasing and convex on [0,1), and the singular near-tangency integral produces the 4/pi² cusp. At r=.4, independent direct point sampling (250000 trials) gave Q=.622992 versus quadrature .622399596, within one sampling standard error. The exact event partition, not simulation, proves the continuum theorem.
